title: qa-repro repro.json — defect-loop evaluator reproduction receipt
description: The ratified output of the qa-repro skill, written to <evid_root>/<key>/repro.json. The runner returns this object verbatim to the control plane as `repro_evidence`; the control plane branches ONLY on `status` and stores the whole object. This file is the single source of truth for the runner and the control plane. See contracts/README.md. v1.1.0: `status` is a 3-value enum so triage can tell a real negative ('not_reproduced' → may REJECT) apart from an undetermined run ('inconclusive' → must NOT reject; retry/escalate). v1.2.0 (additive, backward-compatible): adds an OPTIONAL `media` array carrying capture-time evidence URLs (evidence_store adapter) for the before-video (GIF+MP4) so the control plane can stream evidence at capture time. `media` is never required — a v1.1.0 artifact with no `media` key still validates. v1.3.0 (additive, backward-compatible): `app_map_writes` is now CROSS-CHECKABLE — the kb CLI ledgers every write to kb_writes in the same transaction, so `contracts/validate.py --receipts <KEY>` compares this array against `kb receipt --ticket <KEY>` and reports drift in either direction (a claimed write the brain never received, or a brain write the artifact never claimed). Adds OPTIONAL `brain_writes {ok, failed, queued}` so a run that hit a dead brain or a 429 embedder says so in the artifact instead of the counts silently reading as zero. A v1.2.0 artifact with neither addition still validates. v1.4.0 (semantic narrowing, schema unchanged): `replay_spec` is always 'replay-oracle.sh' (the playwright-cli replay oracle) for a reproduced status; the old 'replay.spec.js' / 'replay-oracle.js' values still validate here, but qa-verify fix-verify refuses them with verdict blocked, reason no-oracle, and the loop escalates.

status.description: The only field the control plane branches on. 'reproduced' = the bug is confirmed to reproduce. 'not_reproduced' = we ran the repro and the bug did NOT occur — a real negative, so triage MAY reject the ticket. 'inconclusive' = we could NOT determine (tooling failed / needs-info / environment broke) — triage must NOT reject; retry or escalate to a human. The skill's finer needs-info-vs-tooling-failed distinction rides in brief.json.outcome_detail (non-contract). The pre-1.1.0 hyphen forms ('not-reproduced') and the collapsed 'needs-info'/'tooling-failed' status values are NO LONGER valid.

surface.description: Defect surface class. One of: pure-backend | presentation/DOM | state-mutation | streaming-agent (a conversational / streaming-response surface).

symptom_quote.description: Verbatim of the observed symptom — never a paraphrase of the ticket title.

app_map_writes.description: app_map rows written to the qa-kb brain this run (selectors/routes/area-tags). May be empty. CROSS-CHECKABLE (v1.3.0): the kb CLI ledgers every write into kb_writes inside the write's own transaction, so this array is no longer the agent's unverifiable recollection — `python3 contracts/validate.py --receipts <KEY>` diffs it against `kb receipt --ticket <KEY>` and reports both directions of drift. Items stay free-form objects (the row, or {kind, area, key}); the receipts check matches on the row's `key` when present and otherwise falls back to counts.

brain_writes.description: OPTIONAL (v1.3.0). What actually happened at the brain seam this run, so a degraded brain is visible in the artifact instead of reading as 'wrote nothing'. `queued` > 0 means the DB was unreachable and the kb CLI spooled the write to the kb outbox (outbox.jsonl) — the knowledge is NOT in the brain yet and `kb outbox --replay` (or the next qa-dream) must land it, so a receipts cross-check will legitimately show fewer ledger rows than claimed writes. `failed` > 0 means a write was refused outright (e.g. version_conflict) and is LOST unless re-attempted. Omit the object entirely rather than guess.

ok.description: Writes the brain confirmed (an `ok:true` response with a receipt id).

failed.description: Writes refused for a SEMANTIC reason — never queued, never retried automatically.

queued.description: Writes spooled to the outbox because the DB was unreachable. Durable on disk, not yet in the brain.

replay_spec.description: Filename of the replay oracle relative to the evidence dir: always 'replay-oracle.sh' — a headless playwright-cli script (never a test/spec file) whose grader, replay-grader.js, sits beside it (a pure-backend oracle has no grader and no browser). Run as `APP_URL=<url> [ROLE=<a role from adapters.auth_provider.config.roles>|none] bash replay-oracle.sh`: exit 0 = correct behavior (GREEN), 1 = bug present (RED), 2 = could not run (BLOCKED, never read as red or green); it prints one JSON line {pass, observed}. qa-repro only names it after seeing exit 1 on the buggy build. Empty string when status is not 'reproduced'.

media.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2.0). Capture-time evidence media uploaded through the evidence_store adapter, each a URL the control plane can fetch directly (Content-Type video/mp4 | image/gif; a signed read URL, or a local file:// URL from the `local` provider — never one that needs an Authorization header). qa-repro emits the before-video pair (before-gif + before-mp4). Omitted entirely when upload is not configured or failed — media is BEST-EFFORT and NEVER required, so a v1.1.0 artifact without this key still validates. The enum is the shared four-kind vocabulary across qa-repro (before-*) and qa-verify (after-*).

kind.description: Which recording this is. qa-repro emits only 'before-gif' / 'before-mp4'.

url.description: The URL exactly as the evidence_store adapter returned it (a signed read URL, or a local file:// URL from the `local` provider). Fetchable with no Authorization header.

attempt.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5.0). Which attempt of this stage produced the artifact, 1-based. Added because the retry audit had to be reconstructed from session transcripts — no artifact recorded its own attempt number, so a retry was indistinguishable from a first pass after the fact. A retry requires transient-failure evidence; a deterministic failure escalates or changes strategy instead of repeating.

retry_reason.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5.0). Why this attempt happened, when attempt > 1 — the flaky-store match, infra error, timeout or oracle exit 2 that justified it.

timing.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5.0). When this stage ran. Costs microseconds to write and is the only way to tell whether a pipeline redesign still holds months later — without it every duration has to be reconstructed from session transcripts, which do not always exist.
